public.text: The country examples are all cases of progress. Without cases where this approach was attempted and did not deliver, a reader cannot calibrate risk and the guidance is open to the charge of selecting on outcome. The most instructive experiences in this field are the unsuccessful ones.
public.suggestedRevision: Add three documented negative or partial cases, each read against a specific design choice. The United States HITECH programme financed adoption of clinical record systems at scale without obligations to exchange, producing digitised but non-interoperable organisations until information-blocking rules were added a decade later - the strongest available evidence that funding without ordering does not produce interoperability. Germany's statutory electronic record and its implementing body show that a legal mandate without execution capacity and with deadlocked governance produces years of delay. Australia's national record shows that publicly secured availability does not by itself produce use.
